title: Finding a visual style for your game: Tips for beginners
summary: A beginner's guide to game art styles – pixel art, low-poly, cel-shaded, hand-drawn, and more – and five habits for keeping your game's look consistent.
body_markdown:
***A beginner's guide to game art styles, suggested use cases, and five habits for keeping your game's look consistent.***


You already know what a game’s style is, even if you’ve never had to name it. You can tell a blocky, retro-looking game from a smooth cartoon or a movie-like 3D world at a glance. When you start making your own game, that instinct becomes a decision: what should your game look like?


The short answer is that there’s no single best style – it depends on your idea, your resources, and what you think will resonate with your ideal player. What matters most is picking a look that fits your idea and that you can keep consistent from the first screen to the last. This guide walks through the most common game art styles, what each one is good at, and offers a handful of simple habits to help you build a game with a single coherent aesthetic rather than several stitched together.
